title: An agent learns whether the program scratch.open started is running
body:
`scratch.open` (`scratch_open` and `start_scratch` in `src/server/compositor/channels.rs`) answers as soon as decade has spawned the program, or as soon as it has asked the pane's current program to close. The agent learns nothing after that. If the new program crashes on startup, or never opens a window, nothing reports it. An agent relaunching a GUI program after a rebuild cannot tell a good start from a crash without asking the person.

## Proposal

decade reports how a program `scratch.open` started got on.

- With `terminal: false`, the call waits until the program's window lands in the scratch pane, the program exits, or a timeout of a few seconds passes. The result says which, with the exit status when the program exited.
- The last lines of the program's stderr come back with an exit, so a startup crash carries its message.

## Open

- What `terminal: true` should report. The terminal's window arrives whether or not the program inside it starts.
- Whether an agent needs a way to ask about the program later, after the call has answered, for a crash that comes minutes in.
- How long the timeout is.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/7403d304
notes.text: Jack agreed: with terminal false, scratch.open waits up to 5 s for the window or an exit and reports which, with the exit status and the last 20 lines of stderr; with terminal true it reports only that the terminal started; no tool for asking later. He asked for an escape hatch for programs slow to open a window. The timeout bounds only the tool call: a program past it is reported as running with no window yet, and decade still puts its window in the scratch pane when it comes. An optional wait argument, in seconds, lets an agent that knows a program is slow wait longer.
